newsitem.title: USA: Fire hits building near New York's Lincoln Center.
newsitem.headline: Fire hits building near New York's Lincoln Center.

text.p: Fire broke out Tuesday in a high-rise apartment building across from New York City's Lincoln Centre for the Performing Arts, causing several minor injuries, authorities said.
NBC News reported the blaze began in the 28th-floor apartment of 88-year-old jazz great Lionel Hampton, who said he smelled smoke and discovered a lamp had fallen onto his bed.
"The lamp started cooking," the musician told NBC. "I was in the living room ... If it had been two minutes later, I would have been cooking myself."
Fire Department officials did not confirm Hampton's account of how the blaze began and said the cause of the fire remained under investigation.
Smoke billowed and flames leaped from windows of the 42-story apartment building, located on Broadway at 64th Street.
The blaze was first reported at 2:30 p.m. EST in the building known as One Lincoln Plaza, the Fire Department said.
Most of those injured suffered from smoke inhalation, the Fire Department said. Most of the building was evacuated.
